patch.value: Adopt sdk/graph engine and drop the pm graph shell-out

Replace all spawnSync/execFile shell-outs to pm graph/list-all with in-process sdk/graph and sdk/runtime calls. Delete userland re-implementations (cycle detection, path search, topo sort, articulation points, etc.) replaced by SDK functions. Add durable graph cache. Add pm-graph next-work command using computeActionabilityReport + analyzeRelationshipSchedule.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: Landed: the canonical impact engine now runs in-process via sdk/graph runGraph, replacing the 'pm graph <sub> --json' shell-out and the 'pm graph --help' availability probe. Availability is now a compile-time guarantee from the declared peer dependency, so the probe and its degraded fallback are gone; the --include-closed fallback is deliberately retained because the canonical engine traverses only ACTIVE items and exposes no include-closed switch. KEY GOTCHA: runGraph resolves its tracker as resolvePmRoot(process.cwd(), global.path), so an in-process call cannot inherit a workspace the way the shell-out did by passing cwd to the child. global.path must always be supplied explicitly, falling back to resolveImplicitPmRoot(workspace); omitting it resolves against the parent process cwd and reports every item as not found.

patch.value: 95/95 tests green. Verified end-to-end in a live workspace on a 3-item transitive chain: impact returned both downstream items with correct distances and explaining paths on the core-graph engine; --depth 1 correctly bounded to 1; --include-closed still routes to the fallback engine; and an explicit --path invocation from an unrelated cwd resolved correctly, which is precisely the case naive in-process resolution breaks.
Canonical graph engine adopted in-process via sdk/graph runGraph; shell-out and availability probe removed. Remaining item-fetch shell-outs split into a dedicated follow-up.

value.author: codex
value.text:
Review round 1 (Sourcery + DeepScan) applied on the same branch, before release:

1. DeepScan flagged the local `const global: GlobalOptions` in runPmGraph — it shadows the Node.js `global` object inside that function scope. Renamed to `globalOptions`. No behavior change; the shadow was real and would have silently broken any later use of the true global in that scope.

2. Sourcery asked for PmGraphFlags to be derived from GraphCommandOptions so the flag surface cannot drift. Applied as an intersection rather than a plain Pick: `Partial<Pick<GraphCommandOptions,'direction'|'maxDepth'|'limit'>> & { maxDepth?: number; limit?: number }`. The Pick half makes an upstream rename/removal of any of the three keys a compile error here; the intersected half keeps maxDepth/limit as `number`, because the SDK types them `string | number` only to accept raw argv, and this package's parser has already produced real numbers. A plain Pick would have WIDENED our surface and let an unparsed string reach the engine. Verified with a type probe: `{ maxDepth: '3' }` is now rejected, `{ maxDepth: 3 }` accepted.

3. Sourcery's memoization suggestion for resolveImplicitPmRoot was declined: runPmGraph has exactly one call site and each CLI invocation is a fresh process, so the ancestor walk runs at most once per process. A module-level cache would add stale-root risk for zero measurable gain.
